result.catalog_pipeline:
WHERE / WHEN
- Code lives in the pipeline/ workspace: TypeScript executed directly by Node 24.21, with its working state in a node:sqlite file.
- It runs in GitHub Actions as workflow catalog.yml (ubuntu-latest, concurrency group 'catalog', timeout 90 min).
- The main trigger is a Cloudflare Cron Trigger ('0 3 * * *' UTC) in the API Worker that POSTs a GitHub workflow_dispatch using a fine-grained token with Actions: write on this repo only. This is reliable, and dispatch is not affected by the rule that disables scheduled workflows after 60 days without activity.
- A backup GH 'schedule' runs at 03:40 UTC. Runs are idempotent, so a late or doubled run does no harm.
- Modes: bootstrap (once), daily, weekly reconcile (Sunday), and rebase every 28 days (or earlier if the delta chain exceeds 25% of the base).

SOURCES
1) IStoreService/GetAppList/v1 is the only source of truth for which games exist.
   - The Steam Web API key comes from GH secret STEAM_WEB_API_KEY and is sent in the x-webapi-key header, never in URLs or logs.
   - Params: include_games=true; include_dlc, include_software, include_videos, include_hardware = false; max_results=50000.
   - Paging: last_appid until have_more_results=false; results come in ascending appid order. GetAppList v1/v2 have returned 404 since 2025-11-13 and are not used.
2) IStoreBrowseService/GetItems (keyless, undocumented, best-effort) for enrichment.
   - context {language:'spanish', country_code:'ES'}; data_request with assets + release + reviews (+ platforms); include_best_purchase_option=false.
   - 200 appids per JSON GET (the URL limit is about 8 KB).
3) Fallbacks only:
   - IStoreQueryService/Query (keyless, 1000 items per call, sort=2, about 197 calls; region-locked titles drop out), used only if the keyed path fails.
   - The jsnli/steamappidlist dump only as a local dev fixture.
   - Never: appdetails (later, on demand in the Worker), storesearch, PICS.

STATE (pipeline/state.sqlite, stored in R2 as pipeline/state.sqlite.br; checkpoint every 100 calls)
- apps(appid PK, name, last_modified, price_change_number, first_seen, last_seen, missing_since, status active|delisted|removed)
- enrich(appid PK, type, name_es, coming_soon, early_access, adult, unlisted, region_locked, release_ts, cs_text, review_count, review_pct, review_score, capsule_path, header_path, fetched_at)
- projection(appid PK, row_hash)
- kv(watermark, base_version, delta_seq)
- runs

DAILY RUN (about 3-8 min)
1) Delta: GetAppList with if_modified_since = watermark - 3600 s (one hour of overlap). That returns about 3.3k changed games, usually in 1 call. Upsert them into apps; the new watermark is the max last_modified.
2) Enrichment queue: new and changed appids (about 3.3k) plus a rotating 1/7 slice of the catalog (about 28k), so every game's reviews, flags and covers refresh weekly. That is about 157 GetItems calls. From each response:
   - type: keep 0 = game.
   - Localized name: stored only if it differs from the base name (about 0.5% of old games, about 4% of new ones).
   - is_coming_soon, is_early_access, release.steam_release_date / coming_soon_display.
   - unlisted.
   - content_descriptorids containing 3 or 4 means adult.
   - Reviews summary.
   - assets.asset_url_format with the library_capsule and header filenames. Cover filenames are never guessed.
   - success 15 + appid 0 means the app does not exist; success 15 + unvailable_for_country_restriction means region-locked, which is kept.
3) Projection row per game: appid, name, alt_es, year, pop = min(15, floor(log2(review_count+1))), and a flags bitmask (coming_soon | early_access | adult | delisted). Diff against the previous projection to produce the day's delta.
4) Server files: search prefix shards and meta shards (appid >> 12 buckets). Both are content-addressed, so only changed objects are uploaded.
5) Validate, publish, save state, report.

WEEKLY RECONCILE (Sunday, 4 extra key calls)
- Fetch the full GetAppList (4 pages of 50k). Deletions are never reported, so compare sets: appids in state but missing from the list are checked through GetItems.
  - unlisted:true: mark delisted. The game stays searchable and addable, ranked low with a badge.
  - appid 0: removed (a '-' row in the delta).
  - Region-locked: kept.
- Also re-syncs any app whose last_modified differs (a delta that was missed).

BOOTSTRAP
- 4 GetAppList calls, then publish a names-only base within minutes so M1 UI work can start.
- Then a full enrichment in the background: 983 GetItems calls, about 17 min at 1 req/s, at most about 41 min if throttled to 0.4 req/s. Checkpointed. Republish when done.

PUBLICATION (R2 bucket ga-catalog in the EU jurisdiction)
- Uploads go through the S3 API with aws4fetch to <account>.eu.r2.cloudflarestorage.com, using a token scoped to this bucket.
- base/{v}/games.tsv: UTF-8 TSV with columns appid, year, pop, flags, name, alt; sorted by appid; stored pre-compressed with brotli q11. Estimated about 2.0-2.3 MB (a names-only TSV measured 1.80 MiB brotli).
- delta/{base}/{n}.tsv: chained daily files, '+' upsert / '-' removal, estimated 1-2k rows, about 15-40 KB brotli.
- search/{hash}.json prefix shards + search/index-{v}.json.
- meta/{hash}.json buckets (cover/header path, release, coming-soon text, review summary, Spanish name) + meta/index-{v}.json.
- manifests/{v}.json, and catalog/manifest.json written LAST, so switching versions is atomic.
- The Worker serves /catalog/manifest.json with max-age=300 and versioned files with max-age=31536000, immutable, Content-Encoding: br, encodeBody 'manual'.
- Garbage collection deletes objects not referenced by the last 14 manifests.

FAILURE HANDLING
- HTTP: one sequential worker with a token bucket of at most 1 req/s; 20 s timeouts; up to 5 retries with exponential backoff and jitter on 5xx or network errors.
- Any 429: global pause of 5 min, then continue at 0.4 req/s. After 3 pauses, enrichment stops for the day and the queue persists.
- Zod schemas check every response. A GetAppList shape violation aborts the run before publishing. GetItems anomalies mark the run 'degraded' and keep the last good enrichment.
- Gates before publishing:
  - game count within -2%/+3% of the previous run;
  - delta at most 20k rows;
  - at most 100 empty names (18 are known);
  - base size between 1.5 and 3.5 MB brotli;
  - smoke queries on the built index: 'hollow knight' finds 367520 at #1; 'elden' finds 1245620, 'baldurs gate' finds 1086940 and 'counter strike' finds 730, each in the top 3.
- A failed run never touches manifest.json, so clients keep the last good catalog. Rollback: node pipeline/run.ts --rollback=<v>.
- Report: GH job summary plus an HMAC-signed POST to /internal/pipeline-report, stored in D1 pipeline_runs. The Worker's hourly watchdog re-dispatches if the manifest is older than 30 h and flags /api/v1/status if older than 72 h.

CALL BUDGET
- Steam key: 1 call/day (delta) + 4/week (reconcile) + 4 once (bootstrap). At most 5 per day, against the ToU limit of 100,000/day.
- GetItems: about 157/day steady, 983 at bootstrap, plus rare on-demand resolves from the Worker for pasted appids not in the catalog (cached).
- GitHub Actions: about 250-350 min/month (free on a public repo; within the roughly 2,000 included minutes for a private repo on GitHub Free).
- R2: about 1-3k Class A PUTs per day, far below 1M per month.
result.search_design:
HYBRID, LOCAL FIRST. There are two tiers.
- Tier 1 (primary, meets the 50 ms budget): an in-browser index in a dedicated Web Worker.
- Tier 2 (bridge for the first visit and low-end devices): GET /api/v1/search on the edge Worker, over prefix shards built by the pipeline.
- One shared package, @ga/search-core (fold, tokenize, rank), runs in the browser worker, the API Worker and the pipeline, so results are the same everywhere.

NORMALIZATION
- NFKD and strip combining marks (accent folding), then lowercase.
- Drop ™ ® © and apostrophes (baldur's becomes baldurs); other punctuation becomes a space; collapse spaces.
- At query time, roman numerals I-X and the numbers 1-10 are expanded into each other.
- CJK, Hangul and Kana runs (6.3% of names) are also indexed as character bigrams.
- The Spanish localized name from GetItems is indexed as an alias.

TIER 1: CLIENT INDEX
- Data: base games.tsv (estimated about 2.0-2.3 MB brotli) plus the chained daily deltas, parsed only inside the worker.
- The index is built from typed arrays:
  - ids as a Uint32Array; year, pop and flags as small typed arrays;
  - display names and folded names, each as one concatenated string with Uint32 offsets (no 196k separate string objects);
  - a sorted list of unique words plus a Uint32 postings array.
- A prefix query binary-searches the word list and unions postings, starting from the most selective token; the other tokens are checked with indexOf(' ' + token) on the folded string.
- Measured on this PC for an equivalent word-prefix index: 0-0.3 ms per query, 220-330 ms to build, about 16 MiB. Estimate for phones (4-6x slower): about 1-2 ms per query and about 1-1.5 s to build, once per catalog version. The typed arrays are then saved to IndexedDB and restored in about 0.1-0.4 s.
- Substring fallback (measured 7-14 ms brute force on this PC) runs only when there are fewer than 5 token hits and the query has 3+ characters. It is time-sliced, can be cancelled, and appends results after the first ones are shown.
- Typo tolerance comes later: uFuzzy (about 5 ms per keystroke, 28 MB peak) only on zero results, loaded lazily.

RANKING
- Exact folded match +1000; title starts with the query +500; all tokens at word starts, in order, +100.
- Popularity bucket x20 (log2 of review_count from GetItems).
- Released +30 compared with coming soon; delisted -200; a small bonus for shorter titles.
- Adult games (content descriptors 3 or 4) are hidden unless enabled in Ajustes.
- At most 30 rows, plus a permanent last row: 'Añadir «...» como juego propio'.
- A numeric query or a Steam link becomes a direct appid lookup (binary search over ids).

EXPLORAR ('listar todos')
- The worker keeps two orders as Uint32Arrays: by popularity (default) and A-Z (sorted once by folded key, then persisted).
- The UI asks for 50-row windows over postMessage and shows every game (~196.6k) in a TanStack Virtual list.
- Filters: lanzados / próximamente / acceso anticipado. Jumping to a letter uses precomputed offsets.

TIER 2: SERVER SEARCH
- The pipeline emits prefix shards keyed by the first 2 folded characters of every token. A shard with more than 3,000 docs is split by 3 characters, and each 1- or 2-character prefix also gets a top-50 list.
- Each doc is [appid, name, folded, year, pop, flags], sorted by popularity; shards are content-addressed in R2.
- The Worker loads the shard index once per isolate. It reads the shard for the most selective token, from an isolate LRU of about 20 MB or, on a custom domain, the Cache API.
- It filters and ranks with search-core and returns at most 20 results (about 2 KB), Cache-Control public max-age=3600, keyed by catalog version plus normalized query.
- CPU about 1-3 ms, inside the 10 ms Free limit.
- The client uses it only while its own index is not ready (first visit, about 3-6 s), on Save-Data or low-memory devices (saveData, deviceMemory <= 1), or if the user turns off the offline catalog. Requests are debounced 120 ms and stale ones aborted.

REJECTED
- D1 FTS5 trigram: loading 196.6k rows exceeds D1 Free's 100k rows written per day (index writes count too), and the index is 19.2 MiB.
- Fuse.js: 394 ms per query.
- FlexSearch, Orama, MiniSearch: 67-316 MB heap.
- Proxying Steam storesearch / SearchSuggestions: 250-380 ms, mixes in DLC and soundtracks, no CORS.
result.capture_flow:
GOAL: from intention to 'apuntado' in under 3 s, one-handed, with no login wall.
1) Open. The app starts on Apuntar. On mobile the search bar sits at the bottom, within thumb reach; on desktop it has autofocus. A cached restart paints the shell and the library in about 1 s or less.
2) Type 2-4 letters (about 0.5-1 s). Results update within 50 ms per keystroke from the local worker; during the first seconds of a first visit they come from the server shard search instead. Each row shows the name, the year and small badges: Próximamente, Acceso anticipado, Ya en tu agenda.
3) One tap on the row adds the game with Estado 'Quiero jugar', under the deterministic id s:<appid>.
   - Optimistic: a React useOptimistic update, then one Dexie transaction (entry + outbox op). The row animates into the list within 100 ms.
   - Android vibrates briefly (navigator.vibrate(10)). A toast shows 'Añadido a Quiero jugar · Deshacer' for 5 s.
   - The field clears and keeps focus for the next game, so several can be added in a row.
   - Sync to the server runs in the background, debounced 300 ms. The server fills in the cover from its meta shards and it appears on the next pull, about 0.2-0.5 s later.
4) Variants without extra screens:
   - Enter adds the top result (desktop).
   - The row's '...' button or a long-press sets Jugando, Completado, Comprado, Platinado or Próximo at add time.
   - Adding a game that is already in the agenda shows 'Ya está en tu agenda (Jugando)' and opens that entry instead of creating a duplicate.

MANUAL GAMES (non-Steam: PlayStation, Switch...)
- The last result row is always 'Añadir «texto» como juego propio'. It creates the entry instantly with just the title (id m:<uuidv7>, source manual). A platform chip can be set afterwards.
- With no results, typing and pressing Enter twice does the same.

STEAM LINKS AND APPIDS
- Pasting into the bar, or Ctrl/Cmd+V anywhere in the app, is parsed by @ga/steam. Recognized forms: store.steampowered.com/app/<id>, steamcommunity.com/app/<id>, s.team/a/<id>, steam://store/<id> or steam://run/<id>, and bare digits.
- The appid is binary-searched in the local catalog (microseconds) and shown as a single pre-selected match: one tap or Enter adds it.
- An appid not in the local catalog (released today, delisted or region-locked) goes to GET /api/v1/steam/resolve/<id>. That checks the R2 meta shard, then falls back to keyless GetItems, which also works for unlisted:true games. About 200-400 ms, then add.

PLATFORM SHORTCUTS
- Android (installed PWA on Chromium): Web Share Target (manifest share_target GET /share?title&text&url). Sharing a game from the Steam app or the browser opens GameAgenda and adds it to Quiero jugar with the undo toast: one action in total.
- iOS / Safari (no share target): a 'Pegar enlace' button (reads the clipboard on tap) and pasting into the bar. Add to Home Screen opens it as a web app on iOS 26.

OFFLINE: all of the above works offline thanks to the local catalog and the outbox; it syncs on reconnect.
result.user_data_and_sync:
PRINCIPLE: the server is authoritative and the client is optimistic. D1 is the source of truth. Each device keeps a full copy of its user's library in IndexedDB, so reads and taps never wait for the network. Off-the-shelf sync engines were rejected: Zero, Electric and PowerSync need Postgres logical replication plus a sync service, InstantDB is closed to signups and shutting down, Dexie Cloud's free tier allows 3 production users, and Replicache is in maintenance. A small custom protocol is enough for personal lists.

DOMAIN MODEL
- Estado (exclusive): quiero_jugar (default) | jugando | en_pausa | completado | abandonado.
- One-tap flags: platinado (forces completado), comprado, proximo.
- Nota: up to 2,000 characters.
- Dates stamped automatically: added_at, status_at, started_at (first time jugando), completed_at, platinum_at, owned_at.
- Extensible: a new flag is one ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN plus one field in @ga/domain; field-level merge supports it at no extra cost. Custom user labels come later as a separate table.
- Entry ids: 's:<appid>' for Steam (deterministic, so no duplicates across devices) or 'm:<uuidv7>' for manual games; later 'igdb:<id>'.

SERVER TABLES (D1, jurisdiction eu, Drizzle 0.45 schema)
- users(id uuidv7 PK, kind guest|steam, steam_id64 UNIQUE NULL, seq INT, created_at, last_active_at)
- sessions(token_hash PK = SHA-256 of the token, user_id FK with cascade, device_label, created_at, last_used_at, expires_at)
- entries(user_id, id, source, appid, title, platform, cover, cover_kind, year, status, status_at, started_at, completed_at, platinum, platinum_at, owned, owned_at, next_up, note, added_at, deleted, clock JSON {field: HLC}, row_v, seq). PRIMARY KEY(user_id, id), WITHOUT ROWID, INDEX(user_id, seq).
- auth_tickets(ticket_hash PK, challenge, mode, steam_id64, user_id, expires_at, status)
- link_codes(code_hash PK, user_id, expires_at, attempts)
- pipeline_runs
- No email, password or IP columns. last_used_at and last_active_at are written at most once a day to save D1 writes. An add or edit costs about 4 rows written.

LOCAL STORE (Dexie 4.4.7)
- entries: mirror of the server rows plus an overlay of pending changes.
- outbox: ++seq, opId, entryId, set|del, hlc.
- kv: lastSeq, deviceId, HLC state, settings.
- catalog: the persisted search index, keyed by version.

OPS AND MERGE
- An op is {opId uuidv7, id, set:{field: value...} or del:true, hlc}, with HLC = wallMs-counter-deviceId, sortable as a string.
- One merge() function in @ga/domain is used both when the client rebases and on the server: each field is applied only if op.hlc is newer than clock[field].
- Related fields share one clock: status + status_at + started_at + completed_at; platinum + platinum_at; owned + owned_at; and so on.
- Ops are idempotent by construction, so retries and duplicate deliveries are harmless and no dedupe table is needed.
- Invariant repair after a merge: if platinado = 1 but estado is not completado, the newer of the two clocks wins. A newer status change clears platinado; a newer platinado forces completado.
- Tombstones (deleted = 1) win only with a newer clock; adding the game again later brings it back.
- The server rejects an HLC more than 24 h in the future.

PROTOCOL: one round trip, POST /api/v1/sync {since, ops[up to 100], client}. The Worker:
1) validates with Zod;
2) runs a read batch: session plus the touched entries;
3) merges in JS and fills cover/year for new Steam entries from the R2 meta shards (at most 40 per request);
4) runs a write batch: UPDATE users SET seq = seq + 1 RETURNING seq; upserts guarded by row_v (optimistic concurrency, a mismatch is re-merged once); then the pull, SELECT ... WHERE user_id = ? AND seq > since ORDER BY seq LIMIT 500.
- D1 batch() is atomic and counts as one query against the Free limit of 50 queries per invocation, so a sync takes 2 D1 round trips.
- Response: {seq, applied[], rejected[], changes[], more, reset?}. The client applies the changes in one Dexie transaction and re-applies its still-pending outbox ops on top, so local changes never flicker.
- Triggers: outbox change (debounced 300 ms), app start (after first paint), page becomes visible, back online, and every 2 min while visible.
- Only one tab syncs at a time (navigator.locks 'ga-sync'); Dexie live queries update the other tabs. Backoff from 1 s up to 60 s.
- Other devices see changes immediately when focused, otherwise within 2 min; realtime push (Durable Objects WebSockets) is a later option.
- Payload: about 150-300 B per entry; the first sync of a 500-game library is about 25 KB gzip.

ACCOUNTS (no login wall)
- The first add creates a guest user on the server (POST /api/v1/session/guest). The outbox holds ops until the cookie exists. Browsing without adding creates nothing.
- Multi-device:
  a) Sign in through Steam (M2): the SteamID64 is attached to the current guest, or the guest is merged into the existing Steam user with the same merge().
  b) Pairing code for people without Steam: 'Añadir dispositivo' shows a 6-digit code plus QR (10 min, single use, at most 5 attempts, stored hashed). The second device's guest data is merged in.
- A device list with revoke. After about 10 entries, a gentle prompt: 'Protege tu agenda: vincula Steam o añade otro dispositivo'.

RETENTION AND RIGHTS
- Export JSON/CSV in the app (works offline) and through GET /api/v1/me/export; import from an export.
- DELETE /api/v1/me cascades through the user, entries and sessions and wipes the local DB. D1 Time Travel keeps restorable history for 7 days on Free; this is disclosed.
- Purges: tombstones after 90 days (a client that is further behind gets reset:true and a full resync); expired sessions, codes and tickets hourly; guests inactive for 13 months, after an in-app notice.
- navigator.storage.persist() is requested after the first add. Safari's 7-day eviction can only lose ops that have not synced yet, and those are pushed as soon as the device is online.
result.steam_account_integration:
OPTIONAL and always server-side. No Steam passwords or tokens are ever collected, and PICS / the Steam client protocol are never used.

SIGN-IN (M2): OpenID 2.0 'Sign in through Steam'
- This is the only option Steam gives third parties (no OAuth or OIDC). The button uses Valve's official sign-in images.
- The flow uses a PKCE-style ticket, so it also works inside an iOS Home Screen web app or an in-app browser, which have separate cookie jars:
  1) The client creates a verifier (32 random bytes) and opens GET /auth/steam/start?mode=login|link&challenge=SHA256(verifier).
  2) The Worker stores an auth_tickets row (valid 5 min) and redirects to steamcommunity.com/openid/login, with realm = our origin and return_to = /auth/steam/callback?t=<ticket>.
  3) The callback verifies the response with steam-signin 1.0.5: openid.mode=id_res; claimed_id, return_to and response_nonce must be signed; realm match; claimed_id format check; then a server-side check_authentication POST that must answer is_valid:true. We also require the signed return_to to contain this exact ticket.
  4) The ticket is marked done with the SteamID64. The tab or PWA that started the flow calls POST /api/v1/auth/ticket/redeem {ticket, verifier} and receives its own session cookie.
- A captured assertion cannot be replayed for another ticket, and nobody can finish a login or link without the verifier. This blocks login CSRF and link CSRF.
- Runtime: steam-signin uses Node's https, querystring and Buffer, which Workers provide under nodejs_compat (the https client is fetch-backed for compatibility dates >= 2025-08-15). Fallback: port its roughly 60-line verifyLogin to fetch (MIT licence).
- Dev caveat (found by reading the source): its canonicalizeRealm drops the port, so Steam login must be tested through an HTTPS tunnel origin, not localhost:5173.

LINKING
- A SteamID64 not seen before is attached to the current guest, which becomes kind=steam.
- A SteamID64 already linked to another user: the guest's entries are merged into that user (same field-level merge), this device's session moves over, and the guest is deleted.
- Unlinking keeps the user's own entries and deletes data that came from Steam.

DATA STORED
- Only the SteamID64. No persona name or avatar in M2; the UI shows 'Steam ···1234'.
- From imports, only the flags and dates the user accepted.
- The privacy notice says which Steam data is stored and where: D1 and R2 in the EU jurisdiction, processed on Cloudflare's network.

IMPORT (M5)
Always started by the user after signing in, so we 'retrieve a user's data only as that user requests'. This design does not import from a pasted profile URL, which could belong to someone else.
- Wishlist to Quiero jugar: IWishlistService/GetWishlist (keyless) opens a review screen with everything preselected; one tap imports it as ops (status quiero_jugar, added_at = the wishlist date).
- Owned games to the Comprado flag:
  - One call to IPlayerService/GetOwnedGames (key held as a Worker secret, include_played_free_games). Marks existing entries as comprado and offers one-tap adds for the rest.
  - Playtime above 0 is only a hint ('jugado 12 h'). Family-shared games do not count as comprado and are excluded.
  - An empty response means the profile's 'Game details' privacy is not Public; the app explains this with a link to the setting.
- Platinado suggestion: a per-game 'Comprobar logros' button calls the keyless IPlayerService/GetUserAchievements + GetGameAchievements (about 1 call per game, on demand, cached). At 100% it suggests Platinado but never sets it automatically, because the Steam Achievement Sets beta changes what 100% means. PlayStation platinums stay manual, since PSN only has unofficial NPSSO APIs.
- Covers for imported games come from the R2 meta shards, with no extra Steam calls.

COMPLIANCE NOTES
- The key lives only in GitHub and Worker secrets and is sent in the x-webapi-key header.
- Footer: 'Steam y el logotipo de Steam son marcas comerciales o registradas de Valve Corporation. GameAgenda no está afiliada ni respaldada por Valve.'
- 'Steam' never appears in the app name or icon.
result.hosting_and_costs:
€0/month for the prototype on free tiers, plus an optional custom domain at about €10-15/year.

CLOUDFLARE WORKERS FREE
- One Worker serves the PWA through Static Assets, which are free and unlimited and never invoke the Worker; run_worker_first applies only to /api/*, /auth/* and /catalog/*. The same Worker runs the Hono API.
- Limits: 100k Worker requests/day; 10 ms CPU per request and per cron run; 128 MB isolate memory; 50 subrequests; 5 cron triggers (2 used: daily pipeline dispatch, hourly purge and watchdog). Static assets: 20,000 files per version, 25 MiB per file.

D1 FREE (jurisdiction eu)
- 5M rows read/day and 100k rows written/day (index writes count). 500 MB per database, 5 GB per account. 50 queries per invocation (a batch counts as 1), 100 bound parameters per query. Time Travel 7 days.
- An add or edit costs about 4 rows written.

R2 (jurisdiction eu)
- Free tier: 10 GB-month, 1M Class A (PUT/LIST) and 10M Class B (GET/HEAD) operations per month, no egress fees.
- Catalog footprint with 14 manifests kept: about 0.2-0.5 GB.

GITHUB ACTIONS
- The pipeline uses about 250-350 min/month: free on a public repo, and within the roughly 2,000 included Linux minutes/month for private repos on GitHub Free.

CUSTOM DOMAIN (recommended before inviting users)
- Needed for the Workers Cache API, whose operations only work on custom domains, not on workers.dev. Also gives a stable OpenID realm and a real brand.
- workers.dev is fine for M0-M1.

STEAM
- The Web API key is free, but the account must have spent at least US$5 and use the Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator.

CAPACITY ON FREE TIERS
- About 20-40 API requests per daily active user (focus syncs and 2-minute polls, mutations, manifest/delta checks, first-visit searches). That supports roughly 2.5-5k daily users before hitting 100k requests/day.
- D1 writes allow about 25k entry changes per day.
- Session and last-active timestamps are written at most once a day, so polling does not consume writes.

UPGRADE PATH
- When a limit is reached: Workers Paid at US$5/month (10M requests/month, 30 s CPU by default and up to 5 min, D1 with 25B reads and 50M writes per month included). It also allows moving the pipeline into Cron Triggers (15 min wall time) and Queues if wanted.
- No other paid service is in the plan (no Neon, Turso, Supabase, Vercel, Render or Fly).

SOURCES CHECKED 2026-10-28
- developers.cloudflare.com: /workers/platform/limits, /d1/platform/pricing, /d1/platform/limits, /d1/configuration/data-location, /r2/pricing, /r2/reference/data-location, /workers/static-assets/headers, /workers/runtime-apis/cache, /workers/runtime-apis/nodejs/https and /workers/runtime-apis/bindings/rate-limit.
- The npm registry for package versions and peer dependencies.
- The steam-signin 1.0.5 source code.

result.compliance_and_security:
GDPR (SPAIN / EU)
- Controller: the developer.
- Lawful basis: Art. 6(1)(b) (providing the agenda the user asks for) for the account, the library and the SteamID64. Legitimate interest only for short-lived security signals.
- Minimisation:
  - No email, password, real name or stored IP address.
  - The SteamID64 is stored only after the user signs in.
  - Guests are pseudonymous.
  - The pipeline handles only public catalog data, so no personal data ever reaches GitHub.
- Layered privacy notice in Spanish: a short first layer at the first add and at the Steam button, and the full page linked from the footer. It covers:
  - purposes and the data kept;
  - Cloudflare as processor (DPA/SCCs);
  - storage location: D1 and R2 were created with jurisdiction eu, while processing happens at Cloudflare's edge worldwide;
  - retention: sessions 90 days sliding, tombstones 90 days, inactive guests 13 months, Time Travel 7 days;
  - rights: in-app export (JSON/CSV) and account deletion, plus a contact email;
  - covers load from Valve's CDN, which sends the user's IP address to Valve, and a 'No cargar portadas' switch.
- Record of processing activities kept with AEPD's Facilita RGPD.
- Minimum age 14 in the Terms (Spain's digital-consent age; review if it rises to the pending 16).
- Only strictly necessary storage (session cookie, IndexedDB, service worker caches), so no consent banner. No analytics or RUM unless the user opts in.

STEAM WEB API TOU
- The key stays confidential: GitHub secret plus Worker secret, sent in the x-webapi-key header, never in the client, URLs or logs.
- At most 5 key calls per day, against the 100,000 allowed.
- A privacy policy that says which Steam data is stored and in which countries.
- A user's Steam data is fetched only when that user asks for it.
- No implied Valve endorsement: official 'Sign in through Steam' images, a trademark notice, and 'Steam' kept out of the app name and icon.
- Undocumented endpoints are used best-effort and politely: at most 1 req/s, with backoff.

SECURITY CONTROLS
- Session cookie __Host-ga_session: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/. 256-bit random token; only its SHA-256 hash is stored; rotated at sign-in and link; idle and absolute expiry.
- Same-origin API, so no CORS. The Origin header is checked on every non-GET request; bodies must be JSON and at most 64 KB.
- OpenID: signed claimed_id, return_to and response_nonce; realm match; check_authentication; a PKCE-style ticket (5 min, single use, bound to its verifier) against login and link CSRF.
- Pairing codes: 6 digits, stored hashed, valid 10 min, single use, at most 5 attempts per code. The Workers Rate Limiting binding adds a best-effort per-colo limit per client, where the plan offers it; the D1 attempt counter is the strict guard.
- Zod validation on every input: title at most 200 characters, note at most 2,000, at most 100 ops per request, enum states, HLC no more than 24 h in the future. Per-user cap of 20k entries.
- Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' https://shared.akamai.steamstatic.com; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'. React escaping; notes are plain text only.
- /internal/pipeline-report requires an HMAC-signed, timestamped body.
- Least-privilege tokens: R2 token scoped to ga-catalog; GitHub fine-grained token with Actions: write on this repo only; a separate Cloudflare API token for CI deploys. Secret rotation is documented.
- Supply chain: exact npm pins, npm audit signatures, Dependabot or Renovate.
- Logs carry no tokens or IP addresses (Workers observability with sampling).
- Backups: D1 Time Travel, restorable within 7 days, with a restore drill in M6.
result.performance_plan:
RULE: the network is never on the critical path of a keystroke or a tap.

1) KEYSTROKE TO RESULTS, p95 <= 50 ms
- Search runs in a Web Worker over typed arrays: about 0-0.3 ms per query measured on this PC for the word-prefix index, estimated 1-2 ms on mid-range phones.
- postMessage in both directions takes under 1 ms. Rendering at most 30 memoized rows with React 19 takes about 5-10 ms.
- Stale queries are dropped by sequence id. The substring fallback is async and time-sliced, so it never delays the first results.
- Measured with:
  - performance.mark on input and another mark when the results commit (useLayoutEffect);
  - a Playwright test that types 40 real queries character by character with CDP CPU throttling at 4x (6x as a stretch) and asserts p95 <= 50 ms;
  - a Vitest bench of search-core over 1,000 sampled names (p95 under 1 ms on this PC).
- The server fallback is used only for the first ~3-6 s of a first visit. It is debounced 120 ms, budgeted at p95 <= 300 ms on 4G and reported separately: it is the one path not held to 50 ms.

2) TAP TO FEEDBACK, <= 100 ms
- A visual state on pointerdown, then a useOptimistic update in the same frame, then the Dexie transaction (entry + outbox) after paint.
- Sync runs in the background, debounced 300 ms. An undo toast replaces confirmation dialogs.
- Measured with Event Timing entries in Playwright, target p95 <= 50 ms at 4x throttle.

3) INP p75 <= 200 ms
- No catalog parsing or JSON work on the main thread.
- Virtualized lists (TanStack Virtual) for Agenda and Explorar; startTransition for filter and tab changes.
- In e2e, a PerformanceObserver flags any long task over 50 ms while typing or adding, and the test fails. web-vitals 6.2.3 onINP is collected in Playwright runs. Opt-in RUM can come later.

4) FIRST-VISIT LCP <= 2.5 s
- The SPA shell (header, search bar, empty-state text) is prerendered into index.html with inline critical CSS and system fonts, served from Cloudflare static assets at the edge with no Worker hop.
- Initial JS at most 130 KB gzip (React, shell, Dexie); routes load lazily.
- The catalog download starts only after load and idle, so it never competes with the shell.
- Measured with Lighthouse CI on the mobile profile for every PR (target LCP <= 2.0 s) and a bundle-size check in CI.

5) CACHED RESTART <= 2 s
- The service worker serves the precached shell, even offline.
- Dexie reads the library (about 20-80 ms for 500 entries) and paints before any network call.
- In parallel, the search worker restores the persisted index (about 0.1-0.4 s). The sync pull runs after first paint.
- Measured with a throttled Playwright reload: the 'library-painted' mark within 1.0 s and 'search-ready' within 2.0 s.

6) SERVER
- /api/v1/sync costs 2 D1 round trips (batches), with the D1 primary in the EU, close to Spanish users. Target p95 <= 300 ms end to end; this is never blocking the user.
- Worker CPU p99 <= 5 ms against the 10 ms Free cap, checked with wrangler tail and Workers analytics, plus an integration test asserting that no handler does catalog-scale work.

7) DATA VOLUME
- First catalog download about 2.0-2.3 MB brotli, once per 28-day base; then about 15-40 KB of delta per day.
- Syncing a 500-entry library is about 25 KB gzip.
- Covers load lazily (loading=lazy, decoding=async, fixed 2:3 boxes) and are cached by the service worker; the CDN sends CORS headers and a 10-year max-age.

risks.risk: The undocumented keyless Steam endpoints (GetItems, Query) change, throttle or disappear. Covers, Spanish names, coming-soon and early-access flags and popularity would degrade.
risks.mitigation: Which games exist, and their names, depend only on the documented keyed GetAppList. Enrichment is additive, and the last good copy is kept in the pipeline state. Zod contract checks on every response, tests on recorded fixtures and a nightly live canary catch changes. The UI falls back to the title and a placeholder cover. Because of the meta shards, the API never needs Steam while answering a request.

risks.risk: Steam returns 429s or throttles by IP on GitHub runners, which share Azure IPs.
risks.mitigation: A single sequential worker at most 1 req/s, slowing to 0.4 req/s and pausing globally for 5 min on any 429. A daily cap on calls, checkpoints and resume. Refreshing reviews on a 7-day rotation keeps daily calls around 157. Fallback: run 'pipeline --mode=enrich' from the dev PC.

risks.risk: Problems with the Steam key: a ToU breach, revocation, or the account becoming limited.
risks.mitigation: The key exists only as GitHub and Worker secrets, sent in the x-webapi-key header. At most 5 calls per day. A privacy policy that discloses the Steam data. No implied endorsement. If the key path fails, a Query-based (keyless) fallback keeps names fresh.

risks.risk: Cloudflare Free limits shape the design: 10 ms CPU, 100k requests/day, 100k D1 rows written/day, 50 queries or subrequests per invocation, and the Cache API only on custom domains.
risks.mitigation: Handlers stay I/O-bound and anything heavy runs in GitHub Actions. batch() counts as one query. Timestamps are written at most once a day. CPU is watched through analytics and integration tests. Get a custom domain before launch. Upgrade to Workers Paid at US$5/month at about 2.5k daily users or if CPU needs grow.

risks.risk: Bugs in the custom sync protocol could lose or duplicate data.
risks.mitigation: Deterministic ids (s:<appid>) and idempotent HLC last-writer-wins ops. One merge() shared by client and server, covered by randomized property tests and Playwright tests with two browser contexts, including offline cases. Tombstones are kept 90 days, an explicit reset path exists, and users can export at any time.

risks.risk: iOS PWA limits: no share target, the OpenID redirect inside a standalone app, and Safari's 7-day storage eviction for sites that are not installed.
risks.mitigation: A PKCE-style ticket redeem for login, a paste and clipboard capture flow, the server as source of truth with immediate outbox flush, navigator.storage.persist(), an install prompt, and pairing codes as an alternative to login.

risks.risk: GitHub Actions scheduling is best-effort, scheduled workflows are disabled after 60 days without activity, and GitHub becomes a dependency for catalog freshness.
risks.mitigation: A Cloudflare cron triggers the run with workflow_dispatch, plus a backup schedule and an hourly staleness watchdog. Runs are idempotent and based on a watermark, so a late run catches up. Clients keep the last good manifest indefinitely.

risks.risk: Exposure to GDPR and trademark issues, because this is a server product: guest data, the SteamID64, IP addresses sent to Valve through the image CDN.
risks.mitigation: No email or stored IPs. D1 and R2 in the EU jurisdiction. Layered notice, record of processing (Facilita RGPD), in-app export and deletion, purge of guests after 13 months, a switch to turn covers off, no analytics without consent. Official sign-in button images, trademark notice, and no 'Steam' in the name.

risks.risk: Lock-in to Cloudflare's D1, R2 and Workers.
risks.mitigation: Hono also runs on Node. The Drizzle SQLite schema ports to libSQL/Turso or node:sqlite. Catalog files are plain files that any S3 or CDN can serve. The domain logic and search code are platform-neutral packages.

risks.risk: Scope creep: building accounts and sync delays the core value.
risks.mitigation: M1 is limited to the catalog, quick add and guest sync. Steam login comes in M2 and imports in M5, behind feature flags. No realtime push and no third-party sync engine in the prototype.

risks.risk: Catalog gaps or search misses: delisted games missing from GetAppList, region-locked titles, CJK text, typos, roman numerals.
risks.mitigation: Resolving a pasted link or appid goes through GetItems, which works even for unlisted games. Manual games are always one row away. CJK bigrams, a substring pass and numeral expansion are built in. Fuzzy matching (uFuzzy) runs only on zero results.

risks.risk: Tooling churn: TS 7 has no API, @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers 0.23.0 still requires Vitest ^4.1, Drizzle 1.0 is an RC, Node 26 is the new LTS.
risks.mitigation: Exact pins with grouped Renovate updates. Vitest 4.1.12 until the Workers pool supports v5. Stay on Drizzle 0.45. A typescript@6 alias only if some tool needs the API. No corepack, so upgrading to Node 26 is trivial.

result.why_this_wins:
1) This is the only angle where 'works across devices from the start' and 'you never lose your list' hold from the very first add. The server is authoritative, so Safari's storage eviction, a cleared browser or a lost phone cost nothing once the device has synced.
2) It does not trade speed for that. Every read, search and tap goes to local memory or IndexedDB, and the network only syncs in the background. The 50/100/200 ms budgets are met the same way a local-only app would meet them, and the server even improves the first visit through shard search before the catalog is downloaded.
3) There is no login wall. A guest account is created silently on the first add, and Sign in through Steam or a pairing code upgrades it later. That fits 'rápida y ágil' better than a sign-up screen.
4) It is the foundation the next features need anyway:
- Steam import (the key must stay server-side);
- wishlists, notifications and shared lists;
- multi-platform data from IGDB, which is backend-only with no CORS.
An own API, migrations, sessions and EU data residency are already in place.
5) €0/month, one vendor, and TypeScript end to end, with shared domain and search packages. No Docker: workerd/Miniflare gives exact local parity with production on this Windows PC.
6) The catalog is treated as a versioned data product: the pipeline produces immutable files, published by switching the manifest. D1 stays tiny and free, a failed run cannot break clients, rollback is one command, and the files are portable to any S3 or CDN.
result.honest_weaknesses:
- More to build and run than a local-only app: API, auth, sessions, sync protocol, migrations and privacy duties. That is roughly 6-8 extra days before reaching the same UX, plus an ongoing security responsibility for a solo developer.
- The custom sync is simple field-level last-writer-wins (HLC): if two devices edit the same field concurrently, only the newest edit survives. There is no realtime push; other devices update on focus or every 2 minutes.
- Server search is only a bridge. On mobile networks it cannot reach 50 ms (about 150-300 ms), so a first visit gets a few seconds of slower results until the ~2 MB catalog is local. Save-Data users stay on that slower path.
- Coupling to Cloudflare: D1, R2 and Workers limits (10 ms CPU, 100k requests/day, 100k rows written/day, 50 queries per invocation, Cache API only on a custom domain) shape the code, and heavy jobs must live elsewhere. The SQLite dialect means a later move to Postgres is a schema port, not a config change.
- Two schedulers (Cloudflare cron and GitHub Actions), with GitHub as a production dependency for catalog freshness, so runs can be late. Enrichment relies on undocumented keyless endpoints (covers, Spanish names, coming-soon, popularity) that may change without notice.
- Guest accounts keep data for people who never sign up, which brings GDPR duties and a purge job. A guest who loses every device without linking, pairing or exporting loses the list.
- iOS: no share target; OpenID inside standalone mode needs the ticket workaround; native builds are impossible without a Mac.
- Tooling edges: TS 7 has no API (fine here, but it rules out svelte-check and typed ESLint); @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers 0.23.0 forces Vitest 4.1 instead of 5; wrangler and Drizzle move fast, so exact pins and regular updates are required.

result.name: GameAgenda Escritorio Nativo — Tauri 2 + SQLite FTS5 (Windows primero)
result.one_liner: App de escritorio Tauri 2 para Windows con el catálogo completo de Steam (~196,6k juegos) en SQLite FTS5 local. Busca en submilisegundos (0,14-0,45 ms medidos por consulta), permite apuntar un juego con un atajo global en menos de 2 s y funciona offline desde el primer arranque. El catálogo, que necesita la clave, se construye en CI y se publica como ficheros estáticos gratis. Las llamadas sin clave a Steam van por HTTP nativo desde Rust, sin proxy CORS. El móvil se cubre en M4 con una PWA compañera y un relay de sync, y más adelante con Tauri Android.

result.catalog_pipeline:
FUENTES
1) Base documentada (con clave): IStoreService/GetAppList/v1 en api.steampowered.com (nunca partner.steam-api.com).
- La clave va en la cabecera x-webapi-key. Parámetros: include_games=true y el resto en false, max_results=50000; se pagina con last_appid mientras have_more_results sea true.
- ~196,6k juegos (~133,9k lanzados + ~62,7k próximamente) en 4 llamadas, cada uno con appid, name (nombre base), last_modified y price_change_number.
- Incluye juegos gratuitos, para adultos y próximos lanzamientos, pero no los retirados.
- Para más adelante: include_dlc=true añade ~63,9k DLC con 2 llamadas más.
2) Enriquecimiento masivo (sin clave, no documentado, semanal): IStoreQueryService/Query.
- Parámetros: context.language=spanish, context.country_code=ES, sort=2 (appid ascendente), páginas de 1.000 filtradas a juegos y un data_request de release + reviews.
- Sin assets: las rutas de imagen llevan hashes de 40 hex y comprimen mal.
- ~197 llamadas. Se guarda el tipo, el nombre ES, is_coming_soon, is_early_access, steam_release_date, review_count/review_score y content_descriptorids (3 o 4 = adulto).
- Query no devuelve los títulos bloqueados en ES; esos se completan con GetItems.
3) Enriquecimiento puntual (sin clave, no documentado, diario): IStoreBrowseService/GetItems.
- Lotes de 200 ids como máximo por GET JSON, para no pasar de ~8 KB de URL. context.country_code=ES es obligatorio; además language=spanish, include_release, include_reviews, include_best_purchase_option=false y sin include_extra_details.
- Clasifica cada respuesta:
  · success 15 + appid 0 = inexistente: se borra.
  · success 15 + unvailable_for_country_restriction = bloqueado en ES: se conserva con el nombre base.
  · unlisted:true = retirado: se marca con un flag y se conserva para resolver enlaces y agendas.
4) Solo en desarrollo: el volcado diario de jsnli/steamappidlist sirve de fixture o semilla mientras no haya clave. No tiene licencia, así que nunca entra en producción.

CALENDARIO (GitHub Actions, UTC, en minutos impares)
- Lane diario, 17 4 * * *:
  · descarga el snapshot publicado como estado previo (el CDN es la fuente de verdad y el runner no guarda estado);
  · GetAppList completo (4 llamadas);
  · diff: altas, cambios (last_modified distinto) y bajas (ausentes; GetAppList nunca informa de borrados, así que esta lista completa diaria es la reconciliación);
  · GetItems de altas y cambios (~3,3k/día, unas 17 llamadas) y de bajas (~1);
  · nuevo snapshot + delta.
  if_modified_since queda como comprobación barata: una llamada, y si no hay cambios y el recuento coincide, no se publica. También serviría para un futuro carril horario de novedades.
- Lane semanal, 43 5 * * 0: lo mismo + Query masivo (~197 llamadas) para refrescar popularidad y estados de todos los juegos, y GetItems para los huecos.
- workflow_dispatch manual, y modo local «node pipeline/run.ts --lane=daily --publish» con el Programador de tareas de Windows como plan B.

FORMATO PUBLICADO (/v1/, ficheros versionados e inmutables)
- games-<ver>.tsv.br para el escritorio y games-<ver>.tsv.gz para la PWA (se lee con DecompressionStream('gzip')).
  · Columnas: appid, name, name_es (solo si difiere del base: ~0,5% de los juegos antiguos y ~4% de los nuevos), flags, release_day, pop, score.
  · flags: bit0 próximamente, bit1 acceso anticipado, bit2 adulto, bit3 retirado, bit4 bloqueado en ES, bit5 sin enriquecer.
  · release_day: días desde epoch, vacío si la fecha está por anunciar.
  · pop = floor(2·log2(review_count+1)), de 0 a 41. score = review_score, de 0 a 9.
  · Los tabuladores y saltos de línea de los nombres se sustituyen por espacios.
  · Tamaño: [appid,name] mide 1,80 MiB en brotli; con estas columnas se estima en 2,3-2,8 MiB (se mide en M1).
  · Sin portadas: se piden bajo demanda.
- delta-<a>-<b>.ndjson.br: líneas ["u",appid,name,name_es,flags,release_day,pop,score] o ["d",appid]; ~3,3k líneas/día, unos 50-100 KB en brotli (estimado). Se conservan 14 deltas y 2 snapshots completos.
- manifest.json, con Cache-Control corto: schema, version (yyyymmddNN), generated_at, last_success, recuentos, url + bytes + sha256 de cada fichero, min_app y flags de cliente. store_browse:false apaga en remoto las llamadas a GetItems desde los clientes.
- Se publica con «npx wrangler deploy» del proyecto gameagenda-catalog (Workers static assets). Un fichero _headers añade Access-Control-Allow-Origin * para la PWA; si no se aplica, se pone delante un Worker mínimo.

CONTROLES DE CALIDAD (si falla uno no se publica y se mantiene la versión anterior)
- El recuento está dentro de ±2% del anterior.
- Las bajas del día son menos del 1%, salvo que GetItems las confirme.
- Hay 50 nombres vacíos como mucho (hoy son 18).
- El esquema y el número de columnas son los esperados.
- Cada fichero ocupa menos de 25 MiB.
- El sha256 se recalcula después de escribir.

FALLOS
- Timeout de 15 s. Hasta 5 reintentos con backoff exponencial de 2-4-8-16-32 s y jitter.
- Un 429 pausa el worker entero: 60 s, luego 120 s, luego 300 s.
- 401/403 en GetAppList (clave revocada): la ejecución falla sin publicar y avisa.
- Si cambia el esquema de Query o GetItems, modo degradado: se publican los nombres de la base, se conserva el enriquecimiento anterior y se marca bit5.
- El pase masivo guarda un checkpoint (last_appid) con actions/cache y se reanuda donde se quedó.
- Aviso de inactividad: al terminar bien se hace ping a un monitor gratuito (p. ej. healthchecks.io), que manda un email si pasan 36 h sin ping. La app también muestra la edad del catálogo.
- Si el cron llega tarde, se pierde o se desactiva tras 60 días sin actividad, los clientes siguen funcionando con el catálogo que tienen (pegar un enlace o appid resuelve las novedades), y queda la ejecución manual o local.

PRESUPUESTO DE LLAMADAS
- Con clave: ~4-5 al día, muy lejos del límite de 100.000/día del ToU. En M5 se suma 1 GetOwnedGames por cada importación que haga un usuario.
- Sin clave, en CI: ~18-22 al día + ~200 a la semana, a 0,4 req/s como mucho (≈120 cada 5 min, el límite que la comunidad observa por IP) y con un solo worker. El lane diario ocupa 1-2 min de runner y el semanal ~10 min: unos 110 min al mes.
- Cliente: ráfagas de 1 req/s como mucho y 30 cada 5 min sostenido; lo normal es menos de 20 al día.
result.search_design:
OBJETIVO: de la tecla a los resultados pintados en 50 ms o menos (p95). El núcleo de la búsqueda debería costar 1-2 ms (estimado), porque no hay red ni debounce.

1) NORMALIZACIÓN fold() (idéntica en Rust y TS gracias a los vectores de prueba compartidos)
- Quitar ™ ® © ℠ ANTES de NFKD, porque NFKD convierte ™ en «TM».
- NFKD, eliminar las marcas combinantes y pasar a minúsculas Unicode.
- Sustituir ß→ss, æ→ae, œ→oe, ø→o, ł→l, đ→d.
- Todo lo que no sea letra ni número pasa a espacio, y los espacios seguidos se colapsan. CJK y Hangul se conservan.
- Columnas derivadas: norm (nombre base, más « | » + nombre ES si difiere) y norm_na (sin artículo inicial: the, a, an, el, la, los, las, le, les, der, die, das), que se usa para los prefijos.

2) ESQUEMA DE catalog.db
game(appid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name, name_es, norm, norm_na, flags, release_day, pop, score,
     k INTEGER UNIQUE,  -- k = ((63-pop)<<24) | appid → ordena «más popular primero»; appid = k & 0xFFFFFF (al importar se comprueba que appid < 2^24)
     p1, p2)            -- primer carácter y dos primeros caracteres de norm_na
Índices: (p1,k), (p2,k), (norm), (norm_na), (k,flags), (release_day,flags).
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE game_fts USING fts5(norm, content='', contentless_delete=1, tokenize='trigram');  -- rowid = k
Unos triggers mantienen game_fts (delete por rowid + insert) cuando cambian norm o k. k solo cambia cuando un juego cruza un tramo de popularidad, cosa poco frecuente.
Decisiones comprobadas en la documentación de FTS5:
- detail=full es obligatorio: con none/column, el trigram no admite tokens de más de 3 caracteres.
- No se usa remove_diacritics: el texto ya llega plegado, y así LIKE/GLOB siguen usando el índice.
- Las subcadenas de menos de 3 caracteres nunca casan con MATCH, así que las consultas cortas necesitan su propio plan.
- Los doclists se guardan ordenados por rowid, de modo que «ORDER BY rowid LIMIT n» devuelve los n más populares sin ordenar todas las coincidencias.

3) PLAN DE CONSULTA (search_games(q, seq) devuelve el top 30)
a) Enlace o appid, detectado por regex: store.steampowered.com/app/N, steamcommunity.com/app/N, s.team/a/N, steam://store|run|install/N, steamdb.info/app/N o un número suelto. Se busca por clave primaria. Si el appid no está en el catálogo (es posterior al snapshot o está retirado), aparece una fila provisional con el título del slug o «Juego de Steam #N», y GetItems lo resuelve en segundo plano por HTTP nativo.
b) Consulta plegada de 1 o 2 caracteres: WHERE p1/p2 = ? AND visible ORDER BY k LIMIT 30. Con el índice compuesto lee unas 30 filas.
c) Consulta de 3 caracteres o más:
- Los tokens de 3 o más caracteres van a MATCH '"tok1" "tok2"' con ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 400. Es un AND implícito; cada token va entrecomillado y con las comillas escapadas, así que no se puede inyectar sintaxis.
- Los tokens cortos («3», «ii», «vr») se filtran en Rust como prefijo de palabra, con equivalencias entre 1-20 y números romanos.
- Además se buscan títulos que empiecen por la consulta (norm_na >= q AND norm_na < q||U+10FFFF, LIMIT 20). Así un título exacto poco popular nunca se pierde.
d) Reordenación en Rust de los ≤420 candidatos, cargados por clave primaria, por niveles:
- 0: coincidencia exacta (norm o norm_na == q, o un alias);
- 1: el título empieza por la consulta;
- 2: todos los tokens son prefijos de alguna palabra;
- 3: subcadena.
Dentro de cada nivel se ordena por k ascendente (popularidad), luego por título más corto y luego por appid.
Filtros:
- Adultos (descriptores 3 o 4) ocultos por defecto, con un ajuste para mostrarlos.
- Retirados ocultos salvo que estén en tu agenda.
- Los próximos lanzamientos NO se penalizan: apuntarlos es un caso clave.
Cada fila devuelve el appid, el título que se muestra (el ES si existe, con el base como subtítulo), el año o «Próximamente», las insignias y, si ya está en tu agenda, su estado (sale de un mapa appid→estado en memoria).
e) Encima de los resultados, una sección «En tu agenda» con las coincidencias entre tus entradas, incluidos los juegos manuales (escaneo en memoria de unos pocos miles de títulos plegados).
f) Fuzzy (M3), si hay menos de 5 resultados: OR de los trigramas de la consulta con ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 2000, y en Rust se calcula la similitud de Jaccard de trigramas; las de 0,3 o más se ofrecen como «¿Quizás buscabas…?». Alias (M3): un CSV curado de unas 200 siglas (gta, rdr2, cs2, ff7…) que se publica con el snapshot.
g) CJK de 1 o 2 caracteres: p1/p2 + LIKE por fuerza bruta. Es un caso raro; estimado en 10-30 ms.

4) LISTAR TODOS (Explorar)
- Lista virtualizada con el recuento total (196.595 en el snapshot medido).
- Orden por popularidad (k), alfabético (norm_na) o por fecha (release_day). Filtros: Todos, Lanzados (~133,9k) o Próximamente (~62,7k), con los adultos ocultos.
- Páginas de 200 filas por OFFSET sobre índices cubrientes, precargando la siguiente. El peor caso, arrastrar la barra hasta el final, se estima por debajo de 40 ms. Si la medida lo supera, se pasa a columnas de rango densas recalculadas en cada importación.
- Cada fila tiene un botón «+» que la añade a «Quiero jugar».

5) PRIMER ARRANQUE Y CORRECCIÓN
- Mientras el FTS se construye a partir del seed (unos 2-5 s estimados, en segundo plano), la búsqueda usa un escaneo bruto en memoria de las filas ya leídas. En JS, ese escaneo mide 7-14 ms en este PC, y en Rust debería ser más rápido: se puede buscar en menos de 1 s.
- Ese mismo escaneo es el oráculo de los tests de propiedades: para cualquier consulta de 3 caracteres o más, el FTS tiene que devolver exactamente el mismo conjunto.

6) CIFRAS
- FTS5 trigram: 0,14-0,45 ms por consulta (medido en este PC con una DB de 19,2 MiB).
- Carga de candidatos y ranking por debajo de 1 ms, IPC 1-3 ms y render de hasta 30 filas 3-8 ms (todo estimado): unos 10-15 ms de la tecla al pintado.
- catalog.db ocupará unos 30-40 MiB en disco (estimado). Nunca se descarga ya construida (serían 11,5 MiB en brotli): se genera en local a partir del snapshot de ~2,5 MiB.
- Descartados: la búsqueda remota de la tienda (250-380 ms por consulta, mezcla DLC y bandas sonoras, sin CORS) y los motores JS pesados (Fuse.js ~394 ms; FlexSearch, Orama y MiniSearch, 67-316 MB de heap).
result.capture_flow:
Objetivo: pasar de «quiero apuntarlo» a «guardado» en menos de 3 s. Nunca hay diálogo de confirmación; en su lugar, siempre se puede deshacer.

A) ESCRITORIO, DESDE CUALQUIER APLICACIÓN (camino principal)
1. Ctrl+Shift+Espacio, configurable.
- Se evitan las combinaciones con Ctrl+Alt porque en el teclado español AltGr equivale a Ctrl+Alt. Si el atajo no se puede registrar, Ajustes lo avisa.
- El handler Rust de tauri-plugin-global-shortcut muestra la ventana Quick-add, que ya está creada y oculta (no hay arranque en frío), la centra en el monitor activo y le da el foco. Objetivo: 100 ms o menos.
2. Al abrirse, Rust lee el portapapeles una sola vez: solo texto de hasta 2 KB y solo para pasarle el regex de enlaces; no se guarda ni se envía. Si contiene un enlace de Steam o un appid, ese juego aparece como primer resultado, ya seleccionado.
3. Escribes 3-5 letras y los resultados se actualizan en cada tecla (50 ms o menos en p95).
4. Enter guarda el juego en «Quiero jugar», el estado por defecto, con su added_at.
- La fila se marca en el mismo frame (UI optimista), aparece el aviso «Añadido a Quiero jugar · Deshacer (Ctrl+Z)» y la ventana se oculta a los ~600 ms.
- Si el juego ya estaba (su id natural es steam:<appid>), Enter muestra su estado en lugar de duplicarlo.
- Otras teclas: Shift+Enter añade y deja la ventana abierta para seguir; Alt+1…5 añade con otro estado; las flechas eligen; Esc cierra.
5. Juego manual (PlayStation, Switch, retro, físico): la última fila siempre es «+ Añadir “texto” como juego manual» (Ctrl+Enter). Basta el título; se crea con el id manual:<uuidv7>, y la plataforma y la nota se pueden poner después.
Tiempo típico: 0,1 s de atajo + ~1 s escribiendo + ~0,3 s mirando + Enter ≈ 1,5-2 s.

B) VENTANA PRINCIPAL: en Agenda basta con empezar a escribir, o pulsar Ctrl+K. Es el mismo componente, con las mismas teclas.

C) NAVEGADOR DEL PC
- Bookmarklet «+ GameAgenda»: javascript:location.href='gameagenda://add?u='+encodeURIComponent(location.href). Lo recibe tauri-plugin-deep-link; si la app ya está abierta, single-instance se lo pasa a esa instancia. El juego se añade directamente y aparece una notificación con Deshacer en 1 s o menos. El navegador pide permiso la primera vez.
- También se puede arrastrar un enlace sobre la ventana, o pegarlo (Ctrl+V) en cualquier buscador de la app.
- Desde el cliente de Steam basta con copiar el enlace de la tienda: el portapapeles hace el resto.

D) ENLACES QUE RECONOCE: store.steampowered.com/app/<id>/<slug>, steamcommunity.com/app/<id>, s.team/a/<id>, steam://store|run|install/<id>, steamdb.info/app/<id> y un appid numérico.
- Si el appid no está en el catálogo local (porque se anunció después del snapshot o porque está retirado), se guarda al momento con el título del slug o como «Juego de Steam #id».
- El cliente nativo resuelve después el nombre y la portada con GetItems, en segundo plano: en 1 s o menos con red; sin red, queda en cola.

E) MÓVIL (decisión de este enfoque)
- M1-M3: no hay captura desde el móvil. Es un riesgo asumido y explícito.
- M4, PWA compañera instalada (en Android/Chromium, y en iOS 26, que abre como app web lo que se añade a la pantalla de inicio):
  · Al abrir, el campo de búsqueda ya tiene el foco: escribir y tocar «+» lleva 3 s o menos con la app ya cargada.
  · Hasta que el índice está listo (~1-1,5 s estimados en móvil), se puede añadir igualmente como manual; luego se empareja con el catálogo por coincidencia exacta plegada.
- Android con la PWA instalada: Compartir → GameAgenda desde la app o la web de Steam (Web Share Target). La PWA extrae el appid y basta un toque en «Añadir».
- iOS no tiene Web Share Target: se pega el enlace (se detecta al pegar) o se escribe el título. Opcional: un Atajo de iOS en la hoja de compartir que hace POST a /api/v1/inbox con el secreto del espacio.
- Todo lo capturado llega al escritorio por el relay: en cuanto se enfoca su ventana, o en 60 s como mucho si ya está enfocada.
- Después del prototipo: Tauri Android reutiliza la UI React y ga-core. Hay que instalar Android Studio, el SDK/NDK y el JDK, y escribir un plugin Kotlin para ACTION_SEND. Una app iOS nativa queda descartada: no hay Mac.
result.user_data_and_sync:
PRINCIPIO: local-first. ga-core (Rust) es la única fuente de verdad; la UI solo invoca comandos y escucha eventos (entries-changed, catalog-updated, store-meta).

FICHEROS (en %LOCALAPPDATA%/com.gameagenda.desktop/)
- user.db: los datos valiosos. WAL + synchronous=FULL; escribe poco, así que prima la durabilidad.
- catalog.db: regenerable. Si se corrompe, se borra y se vuelve a importar desde el seed. WAL + synchronous=NORMAL y mmap de 256 MiB.
- backups/ y logs/. Los logs no guardan notas ni datos personales, solo tiempos y errores.
- Las imágenes las cachea WebView2 en EBWebView. El CDN de Steam manda un max-age de ~10 años, así que las portadas se ven offline después de verlas una vez.

ESQUEMA DE user.db (migraciones con PRAGMA user_version)
- entry(id TEXT PK, appid INTEGER NULL, title TEXT, status TEXT CHECK IN ('want','playing','paused','completed','abandoned') DEFAULT 'want', note TEXT DEFAULT '', platform TEXT NULL, added_at, status_at, started_at, completed_at INTEGER (ms UTC), deleted_at INTEGER NULL)
  · id = 'steam:<appid>' es una clave natural: el mismo juego en dos dispositivos es la misma fila y no se duplica al sincronizar. Los manuales usan 'manual:<uuidv7>', y el esquema admite 'igdb:<id>' o 'psn:<id>' más adelante.
  · title es una copia del título en el momento de añadir, para que sobreviva aunque el juego se retire del catálogo.
- entry_flag(entry_id, flag, value, set_at, PK(entry_id, flag)) + flag_def(flag PK, label, builtin):
  · de serie: platinado, comprado y proximo;
  · el usuario puede crear los suyos («En físico», «Regalo»…), así que el «etc.» no necesita migraciones.
- store_cache, en catalog.db: cover, header, name_es, review_label, release_text y fetched_at. Caducidad de 30 días y LRU de 50 MB.
- kv: ajustes. El steamID64 se guarda solo en local.
- M4: field_clock(entry_id, field, hlc) y outbox(seq, op, pushed).

REGLAS
- Estado exclusivo: Quiero jugar (por defecto) | Jugando | En pausa | Completado | Abandonado.
- Platinado ⇒ status = Completado, y rellena completed_at si faltaba.
- Comprado y Próximo son ejes independientes del estado; Próximo sube el juego al principio de Quiero jugar.
- Las fechas se rellenan solas: started_at la primera vez que pasa a Jugando, completed_at la primera vez que pasa a Completado, y set_at en cada flag. Se pueden editar en la ficha.
- Sin confirmaciones: cada cambio devuelve un undo_id (pila de 20 operaciones inversas), con un aviso «Deshacer» durante 6 s y Ctrl+Z. Borrar solo marca deleted_at; la purga real se hace a los 30 días.
- Comandos: add_entry, update_entry, set_flag, remove_entry, undo, list_entries, export_json, import_json.

COPIAS Y PORTABILIDAD
- VACUUM INTO diario a backups/user-AAAAMMDD.db, con 7 rotativas, y otra antes de cada migración.
- Copia opcional a una carpeta elegida por el usuario (p. ej. OneDrive).
- Exportar e importar JSON con el formato gameagenda/v1: entradas, flags, notas y fechas. Al importar se fusiona por id. Esto cubre también la portabilidad que exige el RGPD.

SYNC (M4; opcional y desactivada por defecto)
No se usa un motor de sync: Zero, Electric y PowerSync piden Postgres con replicación lógica, InstantDB va a cerrar, Dexie Cloud gratis solo admite 3 usuarios y Replicache está en mantenimiento. En su lugar, un relay mínimo:
- Espacio seudónimo: el escritorio genera un secreto de 256 bits, y space_id = sha256(secreto). Se empareja con un QR o el enlace https://<app>/#/pair?s=…; el fragmento no llega al servidor. Sin cuentas, emails ni contraseñas.
- Operaciones: {op_id, entity, id, field, value, hlc, device}. HLC = milisegundos físicos + contador + dispositivo. Gana la última escritura (LWW) por campo, por flag y también para deleted_at. Deshacer es una operación más.
- Worker:
  · POST /api/v1/sync/push (hasta 200 operaciones);
  · GET /api/v1/sync/pull?after=<seq> (hasta 500);
  · DELETE /api/v1/sync/space (borrado total).
  En D1: op(space_id, seq AUTOINCREMENT, op_id UNIQUE, body, created_at), con índice (space_id, seq). Autenticación con «Authorization: Bearer <secreto>»; el servidor solo guarda el hash.
- Ritmo: al arrancar, tras cada cambio (con 2 s de espera), cada 60 s con la ventana enfocada, cada 10 min en la bandeja y, en la PWA, en cada visibilitychange. Salen unos cientos de peticiones al día por usuario activo, muy por debajo de las 100k/día del plan gratuito.
- Cifrado de extremo a extremo (AES-GCM con una clave derivada del secreto): queda en el backlog. En el prototipo hay TLS, cifrado en reposo de Cloudflare y minimización de datos.
- PWA: Dexie 4.4.7, navigator.storage.persist() y exportación. Safari borra el almacenamiento de las webs no instaladas tras 7 días sin uso, así que la sync hace de red de seguridad.
result.steam_account_integration:
Es opcional, llega en M5 y siempre se activa a petición del usuario: el ToU exige obtener los datos de un usuario solo cuando él lo pide. Nunca se piden contraseñas ni tokens de Steam, nunca se usa PICS ni el protocolo del cliente, y nunca partner.steam-api.com.

NIVEL 0 (siempre): sin cuenta. El catálogo y los enlaces no necesitan nada más.

NIVEL 1 — «Conectar perfil sin iniciar sesión» (nativo y sin clave)
- El usuario pega steamcommunity.com/profiles/<id64> o /id/<vanity>. Rust resuelve la vanity con /id/<vanity>/?xml=1 y obtiene el steamID64, que se guarda solo en el kv local.
- Lista de deseos: IWishlistService/GetWishlist (sin clave, 1 llamada). Abre un asistente del tipo «Añadir 87 juegos de tu lista de deseos a Quiero jugar», con casillas y sin duplicados; los juegos que ya estaban no cambian.
- Logros, con un botón en la ficha de cada juego: IPlayerService/GetUserAchievements + GetGameAchievements (2 llamadas por juego).
  · Si están todos, la app SUGIERE «¿Marcar como Platinado?», nunca lo hace sola: la beta de Achievement Sets (octubre de 2026) cambia lo que significa tener el 100%.
  · Comprobación masiva opcional en segundo plano, a 1 req/s como mucho (500 juegos ≈ 17 min).
- Hace falta que el perfil y los detalles de juego sean públicos; si no, la app explica cómo cambiarlo.

NIVEL 2 — «Iniciar sesión a través de Steam», para marcar Comprado (la clave está en el servidor)
1. Botón con las imágenes oficiales de Valve. El escritorio genera un verifier aleatorio y abre el navegador del sistema (opener) en el endpoint OpenID 2.0 de Steam, con return_to = https://<edge>/auth/steam/callback?c=<sha256(verifier)> y el realm del Worker (en el prototipo vale *.workers.dev).
2. El Worker verifica la respuesta con check_authentication (steam-signin 1.0.5). Si la librería no funcionase en el runtime de Workers, se hace a mano: un POST con openid.mode=check_authentication y la comprobación de is_valid y del claimed_id, unas 40 líneas.
3. Con el steamID64 ya verificado, llama a GetOwnedGames con la clave (secret del Worker, cabecera x-webapi-key), guarda {appid, playtime} en D1 con caducidad de 10 min y redirige a gameagenda://steam/linked?c=….
4. El escritorio recoge el resultado una sola vez presentando el verifier, al estilo PKCE (otra app que intercepte el deep link no puede canjearlo), y el Worker borra la fila. El servidor no conserva nada.
5. Qué se hace con los datos:
- Marca Comprado en las entradas que ya tienes.
- Asistente opcional: añadir los juegos sin jugar (playtime 0) como Quiero jugar + Comprado.
- Lo compartido en familia no cuenta como comprado y se excluye.
- Si playtime es mayor que 0, solo sirve como pista, nunca cambia el estado.
- Requiere que los «Detalles de juego» del perfil sean públicos; si no, la app lo explica.
- Las importaciones se repiten solo cuando el usuario pulsa el botón.

TRANSPARENCIA: la pantalla «Datos de Steam que guardamos» lista el steamID64, la wishlist, los juegos, el tiempo jugado y los logros, dice dónde está cada cosa (en este dispositivo; en Cloudflare solo durante el traspaso de 10 min) y tiene un botón para borrarlo todo.

OPCIONAL (escritorio, a validar): detectar los juegos instalados leyendo libraryfolders.vdf y appmanifest_*.acf de la instalación local de Steam. Solo a petición y solo como sugerencia, porque instalado no significa comprado.
result.hosting_and_costs:
M1-M3: SIN NINGÚN SERVIDOR DINÁMICO
- Catálogo en Cloudflare Workers static assets: gratis, con ancho de banda ilimitado y hasta 25 MiB por fichero (el mayor ronda los 3 MiB). Cada usuario hace unas 4 comprobaciones del manifest al día (~1 KB cada una) y baja 50-100 KB/día de deltas. El snapshot completo (~2,5 MiB) solo se descarga tras más de 14 días sin conexión. 100 usuarios ≈ 10 MB/día: 0 €.
- GitHub, con el repo privado:
  · El pipeline gasta ≈110 min/mes y el CI en Linux ~100-200 min/mes, dentro de las cuotas incluidas (unos 2.000 min/mes en repos privados del plan Free; el changelog de diciembre de 2025 dice que no cambian).
  · Las builds de Windows y las releases se hacen en este PC, porque los runners Windows consumen más minutos (históricamente ×2).
  · No se usan runners self-hosted, por la tarifa por minuto que GitHub anunció para ellos.
  · Alternativa: repo público, con cron gratis aunque best-effort.
- Steam: la cuenta de la clave tiene que ser no limitada (5 US$ gastados como mínimo, un pago único si aún no lo cumple) y tener Steam Guard móvil.

M4-M5: SERVICIO OPCIONAL
- Cloudflare Worker + D1 en el plan Free: 100k peticiones/día, 10 ms de CPU por petición y 5M filas leídas/día.
- Las peticiones son casi todo espera de red: verificar OpenID, reenviar GetOwnedGames, leer o escribir hasta 500 operaciones. Quedan muy por debajo de los 10 ms de CPU.
- Unos cientos de peticiones al día por usuario activo dan para del orden de 100+ usuarios activos sin coste.
- Dominio opcional (~10-15 €/año). En el prototipo basta *.workers.dev, también como realm de OpenID.

DISTRIBUCIÓN
- Instalador NSIS por usuario, sin permisos de administrador, de ~10 MB estimados (con el seed de ~2,5 MiB dentro). WebView2 ya viene con Windows 11.
- Firma de código: el prototipo va sin firmar (SmartScreen: «Más información → Ejecutar de todas formas»).
  · Azure Artifact Signing (9,99 US$/mes según la prensa) parece reservado a organizaciones de la UE, no a particulares: hay que confirmarlo antes de pagar.
  · Alternativas: un certificado OV (cientos de euros al año) o la Microsoft Store.
- Android (M6): Google Play, 25 US$ en un único pago. Apple: 0 €, porque no hay app iOS nativa.

TOTAL DEL PROTOTIPO: 0 €/mes. Como opcionales, el dominio y los 5 US$ únicos si la cuenta de Steam está limitada.
result.dev_setup_on_this_machine:
YA DISPONIBLE (verificado): Node 24.21.0 + npm 11.19.0, git 2.56, rustc/cargo 1.99.0 (MSVC), VS Build Tools 2022 y WebView2 155, que son todos los prerrequisitos de Tauri 2. NO hay que instalar Docker, Python, PostgreSQL, pnpm, bun ni Java. La carpeta C:/Users/lucas/Documents/Programacion/GameAgenda está vacía y todavía no es un repositorio git.

PASOS (los comandos funcionan igual en PowerShell y en Git Bash, salvo donde se indica)
1. git init. En .gitignore: node_modules, dist, target, .env*, *.db y *.key. Crear un repo privado en GitHub.
2. Raíz:
- npm init -y y, en package.json, "workspaces": ["apps/*","packages/*","pipeline"].
- npm i -D typescript@7.0.2 @biomejs/biome@2.6.3 vitest@5.0.5 y después npx biome init.
- Cargo.toml de la raíz: [workspace] resolver = "3", members = ["crates/ga-core", "apps/desktop/src-tauri"].
3. UI:
- npm create vite@latest apps/desktop -- --template react-ts.
- Fijar react/react-dom 19.3.1, vite 8.3.5 y @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1.2.
- npm i -w apps/desktop @tauri-apps/api@2.12.4 @tanstack/react-virtual@3.14.23.
- npm i -D -w apps/desktop @tauri-apps/cli@2.12.4: CLI local fijada, sin cargo install.
4. Tauri:
- cd apps/desktop; npx tauri init --ci -A GameAgenda -W GameAgenda -D ../dist -P http://localhost:5173 --before-dev-command "npm run dev" --before-build-command "npm run build".
- En tauri.conf.json:
  · identifier com.gameagenda.desktop (que no acabe en .app);
  · ventana main con visible:false, que se muestra después del primer pintado;
  · ventana quick oculta;
  · la CSP;
  · bundle NSIS con installMode currentUser.
5. Dependencias Rust. Los requisitos caret 2.x nunca resuelven a 3.0.0-alpha; Cargo.lock y package-lock.json se suben al repo.
- cargo new --lib crates/ga-core
- En ga-core:
  · cargo add rusqlite@0.41.0 --features bundled
  · cargo add unicode-normalization@0.1.26 brotli@9.1.1 sha2@0.11.1 regex@1.13.1 serde_json@1.0.154
  · cargo add uuid@1.29.0 --features v7
  · cargo add serde --features derive
- En apps/desktop/src-tauri:
  · cargo add tauri@2.12.5 --features tray-icon
  · cargo add tauri-plugin-http@2.8.3 tauri-plugin-global-shortcut@2.4.1 tauri-plugin-deep-link@2.6.3 tauri-plugin-clipboard-manager@2.5.0 tauri-plugin-opener@2.7.2 tauri-plugin-dialog@2.8.4 tauri-plugin-log@2.10.1 tauri-plugin-window-state@2.5.0
  · cargo add tauri-plugin-single-instance@2.5.5 --features deep-link
  · cargo add ga-core --path ../../../crates/ga-core
- En M3: autostart 2.7.0 y updater 2.14.1.
6. Perfiles de compilación:
- [profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 2, para que SQLite/FTS5 y brotli vayan optimizados también en tauri dev; sin esto, las medidas engañan.
- [profile.release]: lto = true, codegen-units = 1, opt-level = 3, strip = true.
7. Arranque: npm run tauri dev -w apps/desktop. La primera compilación de Rust tarda unos minutos; después es incremental, y la UI se recarga en caliente con Vite. Opcional: un Dev Drive (ReFS) de Windows 11 o una exclusión de Defender para target/.
8. Clave de Steam: pedirla en steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey con el dominio «localhost» (hace falta cuenta no limitada y Steam Guard móvil). Se guarda en pipeline/.env.local (ignorado por git) y en el secret STEAM_WEBAPI_KEY de GitHub. Nunca dentro de apps/.
9. Cloudflare:
- Cuenta gratuita y npx wrangler@4.154.0 login.

10. Fixture: descargar una vez el volcado de jsnli/steamappidlist para los tests offline (solo en desarrollo).
11. Tests y medidas:
- cargo test -p ga-core, que también corre en ubuntu-latest.
- cargo run --release -p ga-core --example search_bench.
- npx vitest.
- E2E, en PowerShell: $env:WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS='--remote-debugging-port=9222', arrancar la build y conectarse con chromium.connectOverCDP('http://localhost:9222') (Playwright 1.64.1; para CDP no hace falta descargar navegadores).
12. Updater (M3): npx tauri signer generate -w $HOME/.tauri/gameagenda.key. La clave privada se queda fuera del repo, en un gestor de contraseñas.
13. Más adelante (M6), Android:
